The *Paccuppannavāra* (Ya 10.3.1) is a canonical Abhidhamma section located within the *Yamaka*, specifically forming the section on the present temporal period in the *Indriyayamaka* (the tenth major division of the work) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language for this leaf text [SuttaCentral]. None of the available secondary literature passages directly discuss this section, matching only the general philosophical term *paccuppanna* ("present") or the narrative *paccuppanna-vatthu* convention in Jātaka literature.
According to DharmaNexus machine alignments, the *Paccuppannavāra* exhibits extensive internal text reuse across the Pali canon, recording 2,105 matches across 25 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its highest density of formulaic overlap occurs with adjacent temporal subsections of the same division: the *Paccuppannānāgatavāra* (Ya 10.3.5; 347 matches), the *Paccuppannātītavāra* (Ya 10.3.4; 287 matches), the *Atītānāgatavāra* (Ya 10.3.6; 398 matches), the *Anāgatavāra* (Ya 10.3.3; 343 matches), and the *Atītavāra* (Ya 10.3.2; 217 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Additional substantial reuse connects it to the *Anusayayamaka* (specifically the *Pariññāvāra*, Ya 7.2.4, and *Pajahanavāra*, Ya 7.2.3) and the *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus detects conceptual and terminology overlaps with Sanskrit and Tibetan Abhidharma literature, notably Vīryaśrīdatta's *Arthaviniścayasūtra-nibandhana* and Tibetan translations of the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā Lakṣaṇānusāriṇī* (D4093) and *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4090) [DharmaNexus].
